messages.content:
You are an extraction engine. You read source code of an existing LLM agent and report,
as strict JSON, only what that source actually says.

Hard rules, in priority order:
1. NEVER invent a system prompt, a tool schema, a model name, a parameter or an eval case
   that is not traceable to a line of the evidence you were given.
2. Cite everything. Every claim carries "citation": "<path>:<line>" using the exact paths
   and line numbers shown in the evidence headers and gutters.
3. When the evidence does not settle something, say so: set "status": "undetermined" (or
   omit the item entirely) and add an entry to "undetermined" with a pointer to the file
   that would answer it. An honest hole is a correct answer; a plausible guess is a bug.
4. Mark text "verbatim" ONLY when the exact characters appear in the cited file. Text you
   assembled from a template, or filled placeholders in, is "templated". Text you wrote is
   "inferred". Verbatim claims are checked mechanically against the file; a false verbatim
   claim is the single worst failure mode of this task.
5. Output one JSON object and nothing else. No markdown fence, no commentary.

Extract an upshift agent definition from the evidence below.

Target shape (upshift runs plain OpenAI tool-calling agents: one system prompt, a list of
function tools, a loop over /v1/chat/completions or /v1/responses):

{
  "agent_name": "string, a slug",
  "endpoint": {"value": "chat_completions|responses|messages", "citation": "path:line",
               "status": "found|inferred|undetermined", "note": ""},
  "model": {"value": "string|null", "citation": "", "status": "", "note": ""},
  "params": {"value": {"temperature": 0.7}, "citation": "", "status": "", "note": ""},
  "max_turns": {"value": 6, "citation": "", "status": "", "note": ""},
  "system_prompt": {"status": "found|inferred|undetermined", "note": "",
    "chunks": [{"text": "", "kind": "verbatim|templated|inferred",
                "citation": "path:line", "note": ""}]},
  "tools": [{"name": "", "description": "", "parameters": {"type": "object",
              "properties": {}, "required": []},
             "kind": "verbatim|templated|inferred", "citation": "path:line",
             "backend": {"kind": "lookup|list|create|update|file_read|file_write|unclear",
                         "state_key": "", "id_field": "", "id_prefix": "",
                         "match_fields": [], "text_field": "", "citation": "",
                         "reason": "why this is or is not mechanical"}}],
  "cases": [{"id": "slug", "description": "", "user_messages": [""],
             "initial_state": {}, "expected_tool_calls": [{"name": "", "arguments": {}}],
             "final_message": "", "checks": [{"type": "no_api_error"}],
             "citation": "path:line", "note": ""}],
  "undetermined": [{"what": "", "pointer": "path:line or path", "why": ""}],
  "notes": ""
}

Field notes:
- endpoint: which API the agent's model call uses. `client.chat.completions.create` and
  `litellm.completion` are "chat_completions"; `client.responses.create` is "responses";
  `client.messages.create` / `client.beta.messages.create` (the Anthropic Messages API,
  `anthropic.Anthropic(...)` or `@anthropic-ai/sdk`) is "messages".
- model / params: what the call site passes (model string, temperature, reasoning_effort,
  tool_choice, ...). Report only request parameters, never SDK/client construction args,
  never `stream`, `messages`, `input`, `system` or `tools`.
- Anthropic ("messages") specifics — report the CANONICAL upshift name, not the wire name:
    * `output_config={"effort": "low"}` -> params.reasoning_effort = "low"
    * `max_tokens=2048` -> params.max_tokens = 2048 (a normal request parameter)
    * `tool_choice=...` -> params.tool_choice, in the Anthropic shape, verbatim
      (e.g. {"type": "tool", "name": "search_docs"} or {"type": "any"})
    * `thinking=...` -> params.thinking, verbatim, as the object the call site passes
    * `system=` is the system prompt, not a parameter: report it under system_prompt.
      It may be a plain string or a list of text blocks; when it is a list, report one
      chunk per block (they are joined with a single newline) and cite each block.
- system_prompt.chunks: the pieces that make up the system message, in the order they are
  concatenated; they are joined with a single newline. Prefer one chunk per source literal —
  a chunk is only "verbatim" if its exact characters are in one file, so a prompt built by
  concatenating three literals is three verbatim chunks, not one. If the prompt is a
  template with placeholders that the code fills from config with a known default, use kind
  "templated" and explain the substitution in "note".
- tools: OpenAI function schemas. If the code builds them from decorators, pydantic models
  or dicts, reconstruct the resulting schema and mark kind "templated" with the citation of
  the definition. `parameters` must be a JSON Schema object. Anthropic tools are
  `{name, description, input_schema}`: report `input_schema` as `parameters` unchanged
  (upshift's tools.json is chat-style whatever the endpoint is, and the loop converts it
  back). A schema the code assembles rather than writes out is kind "templated".
- tools[].backend: how the tool's effect could be re-implemented deterministically in
  memory. Use kind "unclear" unless the semantics are mechanical from the code:
    lookup   - reads entries from state[state_key] filtered by match_fields
    list     - returns everything in state[state_key]
    create   - appends one entry to state[state_key], issuing id_prefix + counter
    update   - changes fields of the entry in state[state_key] identified by id_field
    file_read / file_write - reads or writes text files held in state["files"], where
                             match_fields[0] names the path argument and text_field names
                             the content argument
  Anything that talks to a network, a real shell, a database or the clock is "unclear".
- cases: eval scenarios grounded in evidence you can cite — a test, an example script, a
  README usage block. 3 to 6 good cases beat a dozen invented ones; emit zero rather than
  invent. expected_tool_calls is the call sequence the agent should make; checks use only
  these types: no_api_error, tool_called, tool_not_called, state_count, final_state, no_tool_calls_after_success, confirmation_id_valid, response_contains, response_not_contains, response_matches. Check parameter names are exact and there are no others:
  response_contains/response_not_contains take "text", response_matches takes "regex",
  final_state takes "path" and "equals", state_count takes "path"/"equals"/optional
  "where", tool_called takes "name" plus optional "args_subset"/"exact_args"/"min_times"/
  "max_times", tool_not_called and no_tool_calls_after_success take "name".

   66|         self.message_params = message_params or {}

   72|             system=self.system,
   73|             context_window_tokens=self.config.context_window_tokens,
   74|             client=self.client,
   75|         )
   76|

   80|     def _prepare_message_params(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   81|         """Prepare parameters for client.messages.create() call.
   82|         
   83|         Returns a dict with base parameters from config, with any
   84|         message_params overriding conflicting keys.
   85|         """
   86|         return {
   87|             "model": self.config.model,
   88|             "max_tokens": self.config.max_tokens,
   89|             "temperature": self.config.temperature,
   90|             "system": self.system,
   91|             "messages": self.history.format_for_api(),
   92|             "tools": [tool.to_dict() for tool in self.tools],
   93|             **self.message_params,
   94|         }
   95| 
   96|     async def _agent_loop(self, user_input: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   97|         """Process user input and handle tool calls in a loop"""
   98|         if self.verbose:
   99|             print(f"\n[{self.name}] Received: {user_input}")
  100|         await self.history.add_message("user", user_input, None)
  101| 
  102|         tool_dict = {tool.name: tool for tool in self.tools}
  103| 
  104|         while True:
  105|             self.history.truncate()
  106|             params = self._prepare_message_params()
  107| 
  108|             # Merge headers properly - default beta header can be overridden by message_params
  109|             default_headers = {"anthropic-beta": "code-execution-2025-05-22"}
  110|             if "extra_headers" in params:
  111|                 # Pop extra_headers from params and merge with defaults
  112|                 custom_headers = params.pop("extra_headers")
  113|                 merged_headers = {**default_headers, **custom_headers}
  114|             else:
  115|                 merged_headers = default_headers
  116| 
  117|             response = self.client.messages.create(
  118|                 **params,
  119|                 extra_headers=merged_headers
  120|             )
  121|             tool_calls = [
  122|                 block for block in response.content if block.type == "tool_use"
  123|             ]
  124| 
  125|             if self.verbose:
  126|                 for block in response.content:
  127|                     if block.type == "text":
  128|                         print(f"\n[{self.name}] Output: {block.text}")
  129|                     elif block.type == "tool_use":
  130|                         params_str = ", ".join(
  131|                             [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in block.input.items()]
  132|                         )
  133|                         print(
  134|                             f"\n[{self.name}] Tool call: "
  135|                             f"{block.name}({params_str})"
  136|                         )
  137| 
  138|             await self.history.add_message(
  139|                 "assistant", response.content, response.usage
  140|             )
  141| 
  142|             if tool_calls:
  143|                 tool_results = await execute_tools(
  144|                     tool_calls,
  145|                     tool_dict,
  146|                 )
  147|                 if self.verbose:
  148|                     for block in tool_results:
  149|                         print(
  150|                             f"\n[{self.name}] Tool result: "
  151|                             f"{block.get('content')}"
  152|                         )
  153|                 await self.history.add_message("user", tool_results)
  154|             else:
  155|                 return response
  156| 
  157|     async def run_async(self, user_input: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
  158|         """Run agent with MCP tools asynchronously."""
  159|         async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
  160|             original_tools = list(self.tools)
  161| 
  162|             try:
  163|                 mcp_tools = await setup_mcp_connections(
  164|                     self.mcp_servers, stack
  165|                 )
  166|                 self.tools.extend(mcp_tools)
  167|                 return await self._agent_loop(user_input)
  168|             finally:
  169|                 self.tools = original_tools
  170| 
  171|     def run(self, user_input: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
  172|         """Run agent synchronously"""
  173|         return asyncio.run(self.run_async(user_input))

    1| # Agents
    2| 
    3| A minimal educational implementation of LLM agents using the Claude API.
    4| 
    5| > **Note:** This is NOT an SDK, but a reference implementation of key concepts
    6| 
    7| ## Overview & Core Components
    8| 
    9| This repo demonstrates how to [build effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) with the Claude API. It shows how sophisticated AI behaviors can emerge from a simple foundation: LLMs using tools in a loop. This implementation is not prescriptive - the core logic is <300 lines of code and deliberately lacks production features. Feel free to translate these patterns to your language and production stack ([Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/claude-code/overview) can help!)
   10| 
   11| It contains three components:
   12| 
   13| - `agent.py`: Manages Claude API interactions and tool execution
   14| - `tools/`: Tool implementations (both native and MCP tools)
   15| - `utils/`: Utilities for message history and MCP server connections
   16| 
   17| ## Usage
   18| 
   19| ```python
   20| from agents.agent import Agent
   21| from agents.tools.think import ThinkTool
   22| 
   23| # Create an agent with both local tools and MCP server tools
   24| agent = Agent(
   25|     name="MyAgent",
   26|     system="You are a helpful assistant.",
   27|     tools=[ThinkTool()],  # Local tools
   28|     mcp_servers=[
   29|         {
   30|             "type": "stdio",
   31|             "command": "python",
   32|             "args": ["-m", "mcp_server"],
   33|         },
   34|     ]
   35| )
   36| 
   37| # Run the agent
   38| response = agent.run("What should I consider when buying a new laptop?")
   39| ```
   40| 
   41| From this foundation, you can add domain-specific tools, optimize performance, or implement custom response handling. We remain deliberately unopinionated - this backbone simply gets you started with fundamentals.
   42| 
   43| ## Requirements
   44| 
   45| - Python 3.8+
   46| - Claude API key (set as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable)
   47| - `anthropic` Python library
   48| - `mcp` Python library

   29| ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   30|     """Execute multiple tools sequentially or in parallel."""
   31|

   51|         if isinstance(content, str):
   52|             content = [{"type": "text", "text": content}]
   53|

   55|         self.messages.append(message)

   60|                 + getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0)
   61|                 + getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0)
   62|             )
   63|             output_tokens = usage.output_tokens
   64| 
   65|             current_turn_input = total_input - self.total_tokens
   66|             self.message_tokens.append((current_turn_input, output_tokens))
   67|             self.total_tokens += current_turn_input + output_tokens

   71|         if self.total_tokens <= self.context_window_tokens:
   72|             return
   73| 
   74|         TRUNCATION_NOTICE_TOKENS = 25
   75|         TRUNCATION_MESSAGE = {

   77|             "content": [

   81|                 }

   87|             self.messages.pop(0)

   91|                 self.total_tokens -= input_tokens + output_tokens
   92| 
   93|         while (
   94|             self.message_tokens
   95|             and len(self.messages) >= 2
   96|             and self.total_tokens > self.context_window_tokens
   97|         ):
   98|             remove_message_pair()

  100|             if self.messages and self.message_tokens:
  101|                 original_input_tokens, original_output_tokens = (
  102|                     self.message_tokens[0]
  103|                 )
  104|                 self.messages[0] = TRUNCATION_MESSAGE
  105|                 self.message_tokens[0] = (

   14| class MCPConnection(ABC):
   15|     """Base class for MCP server connections."""
   16| 
   17|     def __init__(self):
   18|         self.session = None
   19|         self._rw_ctx = None
   20|         self._session_ctx = None
   21| 
   22|     @abstractmethod
   23|     async def _create_rw_context(self):
   24|         """Create the read/write context based on connection type."""
   25| 
   26|     async def __aenter__(self):
   27|         """Initialize MCP server connection."""
   28|         self._rw_ctx = await self._create_rw_context()
   29|         read_write = await self._rw_ctx.__aenter__()
   30|         read, write = read_write
   31|         self._session_ctx = ClientSession(read, write)
   32|         self.session = await self._session_ctx.__aenter__()
   33|         await self.session.initialize()
   34|         return self
   35| 
   36|     async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
   37|         """Clean up MCP server connection resources."""
   38|         try:
   39|             if self._session_ctx:
   40|                 await self._session_ctx.__aexit__(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb)
   41|             if self._rw_ctx:
   42|                 await self._rw_ctx.__aexit__(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb)
   43|         except Exception as e:
   44|             print(f"Error during cleanup: {e}")
   45|         finally:
   46|             self.session = None
   47|             self._session_ctx = None
   48|             self._rw_ctx = None
   49| 
   50|     async def list_tools(self) -> Any:
   51|         """Retrieve available tools from the MCP server."""
   52|         response = await self.session.list_tools()
   53|         return response.tools
   54| 
   55|     async def call_tool(
   56|         self, tool_name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]
   57|     ) -> Any:
   58|         """Call a tool on the MCP server with provided arguments."""
   59|         return await self.session.call_tool(tool_name, arguments=arguments)
   60|

   62| class MCPConnectionStdio(MCPConnection):
   63|     """MCP connection using standard input/output."""
   64| 
   65|     def __init__(
   66|         self, command: str, args: list[str] = [], env: dict[str, str] = None
   67|     ):
   68|         super().__init__()
   69|         self.command = command
   70|         self.args = args
   71|         self.env = env
   72| 
   73|     async def _create_rw_context(self):
   74|         return stdio_client(

   81| class MCPConnectionSSE(MCPConnection):
   82|     """MCP connection using Server-Sent Events."""
   83| 
   84|     def __init__(self, url: str, headers: dict[str, str] = None):
   85|         super().__init__()
   86|         self.url = url
   87|         self.headers = headers or {}
   88| 
   89|     async def _create_rw_context(self):
   90|         return sse_client(url=self.url, headers=self.headers)
   91| 
   92| 
   93| def create_mcp_connection(config: dict[str, Any]) -> MCPConnection:
   94|     """Factory function to create the appropriate MCP connection."""
   95|     conn_type = config.get("type", "stdio").lower()
   96| 
   97|     if conn_type == "stdio":
   98|         if not config.get("command"):
   99|             raise ValueError("Command is required for STDIO connections")
  100|         return MCPConnectionStdio(
  101|             command=config["command"],
  102|             args=config.get("args"),
  103|             env=config.get("env"),
  104|         )
  105| 
  106|     elif conn_type == "sse":
  107|         if not config.get("url"):
  108|             raise ValueError("URL is required for SSE connections")
  109|         return MCPConnectionSSE(
  110|             url=config["url"], headers=config.get("headers")
  111|         )
  112| 
  113|     else:
  114|         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported connection type: {conn_type}")
  115| 
  116| 
  117| async def setup_mcp_connections(
  118|     mcp_servers: list[dict[str, Any]] | None,
  119|     stack: AsyncExitStack,
  120| ) -> list[MCPTool]:
  121|     """Set up MCP server connections and create tool interfaces."""
  122|     if not mcp_servers:
  123|         return []
  124| 
  125|     mcp_tools = []
  126| 
  127|     for config in mcp_servers:
  128|         try:
  129|             connection = create_mcp_connection(config)
  130|             await stack.enter_async_context(connection)
  131|             tool_definitions = await connection.list_tools()
  132| 
  133|             for tool_info in tool_definitions:
  134|                 mcp_tools.append(
  135|                     MCPTool(
  136|                         name=tool_info.name,
  137|                         description=tool_info.description
  138|                         or f"MCP tool: {tool_info.name}",
  139|                         input_schema=tool_info.inputSchema,
  140|                         connection=connection,
  141|                     )
  142|                 )
  143| 
  144|         except Exception as e:
  145|             print(f"Error setting up MCP server {config}: {e}")
  146| 
  147|     print(
  148|         f"Loaded {len(mcp_tools)} MCP tools from {len(mcp_servers)} servers."
  149|     )
  150|     return mcp_tools
